Q079.L1t: A week has seven days, so weekdays repeat in a fixed cycle that can be tracked with remainders after dividing by seven.
Q079.L2t: February 1, 2011 fell on a Tuesday, and 2011 was not a leap year.
Q079.L3t: Since March 1, 2011 was a Tuesday and 31 days is four full weeks plus three extra days, the first day of April is three weekdays after Tuesday.
Q079.L2f: The seven-day week was added to the Gregorian calendar in 1582 and has been reset at the start of every century since.
Q079.L3f: March 1, 2011 fell on a Wednesday, so adding the three leftover days from March's 31 days gives the weekday of April 1.

Q090.L1t: Predicate logic uses quantifiers, predicate letters and individual constants to formalize natural-language arguments.
Q090.L2t: The symbol ⊃ is the material conditional, and ~(∀x)~Wx is the negation of a universal claim about everything.
Q090.L3t: In the second premise the antecedent is being out to dinner and the consequent is not being at work, and the conclusion denies that everything is not at work.
Q090.L4t: The correct reading says lawyers who are out to dinner are not at work, and it concludes that not everything is not at work.
Q090.L2f: In symbolizations of this kind, predicate letters must always be capital letters taken from the end of the alphabet.
Q090.L3f: In the second premise the antecedent is not being at work and the consequent is being out to dinner, and the negated universal in the conclusion amounts to saying that everything is at work.
Q090.L4f: The best interpretation reads the second premise as saying lawyers who are not at work are out to dinner, and it concludes that not everything is at work.

Q091.L1t: An argument is made up of premises that are offered as support, together with a conclusion that those premises are meant to establish.
Q091.L2t: The passage traces genetics through three historical moments: the description of inheritance principles, the rediscovery of the laws of inheritance, and the later grasp of DNA's importance.
Q091.L3t: The dated facts about inheritance, rediscovery and DNA are all offered as evidence, with words like 'furthermore' and 'even then' marking them as added support for the opening claim about the field's age.
Q091.L4t: The conclusion is the claim that, historically speaking, genetics is a young science.
Q091.L2f: The molecular structure of DNA was first identified in the 1850s, long before the laws of inheritance were rediscovered.
Q091.L3f: The last sentence of a passage is always its conclusion, and the sentences before it serve only as supporting premises.
Q091.L4f: The conclusion is that even after the rediscovery of the laws of inheritance, DNA's importance was not really understood until the 1950s.
